concept.name: National best bid and offer
concept.definition: The highest protected bid and the lowest protected offer for an NMS stock across all national securities exchanges, calculated and disseminated on a current and continuing basis under Regulation NMS; when market centers transmit identical bids or offers, they are ranked first by size, then by time (Rule 600(b)(60)).
concept.intuition: It is the single national reference for the best available displayed prices in a fragmented market where the same stock trades on many venues.
concept.mechanics: Computed from the protected (automated, accessible) quotations of exchanges and associations by the plan processor, competing consolidators, or self-aggregators. It anchors the Rule 611 order-protection obligation and the Rule 605 execution-quality statistics.
concept.formula: NBB = max of protected bids across venues; NBO = min of protected offers across venues.
concept.failure_modes: The consolidated NBBO lags direct exchange data feeds, historically excluded odd lots, and may reference sizes too small to be economically accessible; during locked or crossed conditions it ceases to represent an orderly market.
concept.misconceptions: The NBBO is not the totality of available liquidity - it excludes book depth beyond the inside, hidden orders, and dark-pool interest.
concept.example: NYSE quotes $100.00 x $100.03 and Nasdaq quotes $100.01 x $100.02; the NBBO is $100.01 x $100.02, drawing each side from a different venue.

citations.source: 17 CFR 242.600 - NMS security designation and definitions (Regulation NMS Rule 600)
citations.section: paragraph (b)(60) National best bid and national best offer
